modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Keep separate Type 10 and Type 41 inventories keyed by their native schemas, with an explicit project mapping only if both represent the same physical device set.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes the source/script mismatch auditable and prevents silent schema substitution.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Detects missing legacy Type 10 entries and distinguishes them from extended Type 41 device instances.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Some platforms legitimately expose only one type; absence cannot be judged until platform policy resolves the expected schema.

project_override_considerations: Project SPEC may select Type 10, Type 41 or both, but must record which source coverage is waived or mapped and cannot treat a different schema as automatic equivalence.

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and command require SMBIOS Type 10, while the source Script path names Type 41. These are distinct SMBIOS structures, so the script cannot be silently treated as the requested method.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The purpose is identifiable and the conflict can be resolved by a finite project/vendor ruling; review is complete, while execution waits for that input.

review_improvement: Prevents a Type 41 script or truncated Type 10 header from being credited as complete Type 10 onboard-device persistence evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: Type 10 is a legacy onboard-device structure with type/description entries, whereas Type 41 includes extended instance and segment/bus/device/function semantics. The private script name materially changes the schema, so owner mapping is required. Because the finite decision and reboot gate can be supplied, REQUIRES—not BLOCKED—is correct.
